docs.title: My First Day at SLIBTEC!
docs.text: The way I got the chance to join SLIBTEC is still unbelivable. It was 26th Oct 2024 morning, and I was searching for software engineer interns as usual as the last few months. Having a degree in Plant Biotechnology did not appeal to many software engineering companies and I needed to upskill myself to apply too. It has been several months without positive response from anywhere. Before switching completely to seaching SE jobs, after completing the degree, my plan was to do some bioinformatics training and get a entry level bioinformatics position somewhere. But my efforts in applying did not go as expected.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text: Welcome to my Projects section! Here, you'll find an overview of the various applications and tools I have developed over the years. These projects reflect my journey in software development and my passion for solving real-world problems through innovative solutions. Each project demonstrates a different set of skills, technologies, and problem-solving approaches, ranging from mobile apps to web-based platforms and automated tools.

docs.title: Project List
docs.text:
1. Rental Management Dashboard An admin dashboard for managing a power tool rental business, with React, Django, and plans for WooCommerce integration.

  2. Cancer Cell Image Segmentation

  3. Sporify - Automating Fungal Spore Measurements A Python-based GUI application to automate the measurement of fungal spores using OpenCV and PIL. Designed for my research on Pestalotiopsis fungi.

  4. Car Price Scraper - Automating Price Comparison A data scraping tool to compare car prices across two popular classified sites in Sri Lanka. Built with a Tkinter-based GUI and plans to evolve into a web application.

  5. MycoDataLab - Data Management for Biological Research A data management software built for organizing research data in biological studies. It uses a modular approach with customizable data fields defined by JSON schemas.

  6. ImageCropp - Automated Image Cropping and Annotation A Python-based application to automate image cropping and scale bar annotations, using Tkinter and PIL to facilitate scientific research.

  7. BIT Pastpapers App v1.0.0 An Android app created to centralize past papers for BIT students, built using Apache Cordova with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

  8. BIT Pastpapers App v2.0.0 An improved version of the BIT Pastpapers App with enhanced UI and responsive document viewing capabilities.

  9. Community Managed Boarding Database A web-based database developed to help university students find boarding places easily, built with HTML, Bootstrap, jQuery, and PHP.

  10. WhatsApp Bot for Storing Lecture Recording Links A PHP-based WhatsApp bot for managing and retrieving lecture recording links shared within university WhatsApp groups.

  11. SabraPoems - Android App for Literature Enthusiasts My first Android app, created to assist students at Sabaragamuwa University with their English Literature course by providing a collection of recommended poems and links to resources.

Each project represents a unique challenge and a learning experience in my journey as a developer. Click on the project titles to learn more about each of them!

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The BIT Pastpapers App v1.0.0 was developed in 2019 as a solution to address the lack of a centralized, easily accessible collection of past papers for students pursuing the Bachelor of Information Technology (BIT) external degree at UCSC, University of Colombo. During my studies, I identified a significant gap—students needed a convenient way to access and review past papers for exam preparation. To bridge this gap, I developed the BIT Pastpapers App as my second Android application.

docs.title: Key Technologies
docs.text:
• Apache Cordova: Utilized to build the app as a cross-platform solution.
  • Pure HTML: For structuring the app’s content.
  • Pure CSS: For styling and ensuring a clean, minimalist user interface.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
1. Collection of Past Papers and Answer Sheets The app provides a centralized collection of past papers along with their corresponding answer sheets. Students can access these documents in one place, making it easier to prepare for exams.

  2. Simple and Intuitive Interface The app was designed with a simple and user-friendly interface, allowing students to quickly find and open the past papers and answer sheets without navigating through complex menus.

  3. Offline Access Once the past papers are downloaded, they can be accessed offline, making it convenient for students to study even when they don’t have internet connectivity.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
The initial version of the app had a few drawbacks, mainly due to its development using Apache Cordova and the reliance on pure HTML and CSS. These included:

  • Non-Resizable Content: The past papers and answer sheets were displayed in a non-resizable format, which could be a challenge for users on smaller devices or those needing to zoom in for readability.
  • Limited Interactivity: Since the app was built with basic HTML and CSS, it lacked some interactive features that could enhance user experience.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: As a student myself, I understood the importance of having easy access to study materials, especially when preparing for examinations. Recognizing that many of my fellow students faced similar challenges in finding a proper collection of past papers, I decided to build the BIT Pastpapers App to fill that gap.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: BIT Pastpapers App v2.0.0 is an improved version of the original past papers app, designed to offer a more refined and user-centric experience for students pursuing the Bachelor of Information Technology (BIT) degree at UCSC, University of Colombo. Building upon the foundation of version 1.0.0, the new version introduces significant improvements in both user interface (UI) and document viewing capabilities.

docs.title: Key Technologies
docs.text:
• Apache Cordova: Cross-platform app framework for Android and iOS support.
  • HTML5 and CSS3: Enhanced design with a focus on responsive and user-friendly elements.
  • JavaScript: Used to implement interactivity and document handling.

docs.title: New Features & Improvements
docs.text:
1. Improved User Interface (UI) and Design The app now adheres to modern UI design principles to provide a cleaner and more intuitive interface. This update focuses on improving usability and accessibility, making it easier for students to navigate through the app and locate past papers and answers.

  2. Responsive Document Viewer A major enhancement in v2.0.0 is the introduction of a responsive document viewer. Unlike the previous version, users can now resize documents, zoom in or out, and view content in a more comfortable and accessible manner. This change addresses one of the biggest limitations of the earlier version.

  3. Optimized for Multiple Devices The app’s layout has been designed to adapt to various screen sizes, allowing it to provide an optimal viewing experience on both smartphones and tablets.

  4. Search and Filtering Options (Planned) Although currently in development, future updates to version 2.0.0 aim to include a search feature that enables users to quickly find specific past papers by subject, year, or keyword. This improvement will save users valuable time when searching for specific study materials.

docs.title: Motivation for v2.0.0
docs.text: The primary motivation behind this improved version was to address the feedback received from users of the v1.0.0 app. While the original version was functional and met a critical need, there were clear areas for improvement, particularly in terms of user experience and document readability. This new version focuses on enhancing these key areas to better serve students’ needs.

docs.title: Key Enhancements
docs.text:
• UI/UX Improvements: A modern, user-focused interface for easier navigation and a better overall experience.
  • Responsive Viewing: The ability to resize and zoom documents for enhanced readability on different devices.
  • Optimized Performance: Faster loading times and a more fluid user experience through optimized code and layout design.

docs.title: Future Plans
docs.text:
• Search and Filter: Implementation of search and filter options to help users find past papers based on subjects, topics, or exam years.
  • Bookmarking: Adding a bookmarking feature to allow users to save their frequently accessed documents for quick reference.

BIT Pastpapers App v2.0.0 showcases how user feedback and iterative design improvements can lead to a significantly enhanced product, making it an indispensable tool for BIT students at UCSC.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In 2020, during my first year at university, I faced a common challenge with my friends—finding suitable boarding houses near campus. To address this issue, I designed a Community Managed Boarding Database, a simple yet effective platform for students to discover and share information about available boarding places. The goal was to create a centralized, community-driven resource where students could easily find and contribute listings of boarding houses.

The project utilized HTML, Bootstrap, and jQuery for the frontend, while the backend was developed with PHP. Despite not having the original codebase or screenshots, the impact and purpose of this project remain significant to me and my peers.

docs.title: Key Technologies
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML, Bootstrap, jQuery
  • Backend: PHP
  • Database: MySQL (for storing listings and user information)

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
1. Community-Driven Listings The core feature of the platform was its community-driven approach. Students could add new listings of boarding places, complete with essential details such as rent, facilities, location, and contact information. This allowed for a dynamic and up-to-date database, managed collectively by the student community.

  2. Search and Filter Functionality The platform allowed users to search and filter listings based on various parameters like rent, proximity to the university, and available facilities. This made it easier for students to find boarding places that matched their needs.

  3. Responsive Design Built with Bootstrap, the platform was responsive, ensuring that students could access and browse listings easily from both mobile devices and desktop computers.

  4. User-Submitted Reviews (Planned) Although not fully implemented in the initial version, the platform was intended to allow users to submit reviews and ratings for boarding places. This feature was envisioned to help fellow students make informed decisions based on peer feedback.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: The motivation for creating this platform came from personal experience. During the first year of university, I saw how difficult and time-consuming it was for students to find suitable boarding houses. Most information was scattered or outdated, making the search process frustrating. This inspired me to develop a solution that could help not only my friends but also future students facing the same challenges.

docs.title: Challenges and Learnings
docs.text: Despite being a simple project, developing the Community Managed Boarding Database taught me valuable lessons in web development and project management. Working with PHP and jQuery for backend logic and dynamic content rendering was a foundational experience, while using Bootstrap helped me understand the principles of responsive design. Additionally, the project highlighted the importance of gathering and integrating user feedback to improve usability.

docs.title: Project Status
docs.text:
The platform was actively used by my friends during my first year and provided a valuable resource for discovering boarding houses near the university. Although I no longer have the original codebase or screenshots, this project remains a memorable achievement that showcased how technology can address everyday challenges faced by students.

The Community Managed Boarding Database demonstrates the potential of simple, community-driven platforms to solve real-world problems and reflects my early journey in web development.

docs.title: ImageCropp - Automated Image Cropping and Annotation
Overview
docs.text:
ImageCropp is a Python-based GUI software developed to simplify the process of cropping images and adding scale bars for scientific research purposes. During my wet lab research, I often needed to crop specific regions of microscopic images and annotate them with accurate scale bars. Using traditional software like ImageJ proved to be repetitive and labor-intensive, which led me to design a more streamlined solution with ImageCropp.

The application leverages Tkinter for the user interface, Python Imaging Library (PIL) for image processing, and Python as the core programming language.

docs.title: Key Technologies
docs.text:
• Python 3.x: Core programming language.
  • Tkinter: Used to create a simple and intuitive graphical user interface.
  • PIL (Pillow): For handling image manipulation tasks such as cropping and annotating.

docs.title: Features & Workflow
docs.text:
1. Easy Image Cropping Users can open an image, select a region of interest by drawing a rectangular box, and crop it with a single click. This eliminates the tedious, manual effort typically required when using traditional image processing tools.

  2. Scalebar Annotation After cropping, the user can annotate the image with a precise scale bar. The scale bar’s length and label can be adjusted to match the microscope calibration, ensuring accurate measurements in the final annotated image.

  3. Intuitive GUI ImageCropp features a user-friendly interface that provides clear options for image loading, cropping, and scale bar adjustments. Built with Tkinter, the layout is straightforward and allows researchers to focus on their tasks without needing extensive training.

  4. Batch Processing Capabilities (Planned) Future updates aim to include batch processing, allowing researchers to apply the same cropping and scale bar annotations to multiple images at once, saving even more time.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Load Image: Users can load images through the file browser within the application.
  2. Draw Crop Box: A simple click-and-drag motion allows users to define the region to be cropped.
  3. Crop and Annotate: Users can confirm the crop and optionally add a scale bar. The application will ask for calibration details to accurately render the scale bar.
  4. Save Cropped Image: The final cropped and annotated image can be saved in various formats like PNG or JPEG for publication or further analysis.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: The motivation behind ImageCropp stemmed from the need to expedite routine tasks in image processing for wet lab research. Traditional tools like ImageJ were highly functional but often cumbersome for specific tasks like repetitive cropping and adding scale bars. With ImageCropp, researchers can achieve these tasks in a matter of seconds, enhancing productivity and reducing manual errors.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
• Batch Processing: Enabling users to process multiple images simultaneously.
  • Custom Annotations: Adding support for more advanced annotations like labels, arrows, and shapes.
  • Extended Scalebar Options: Providing users with customizable options for scalebar placement, color, and style.

ImageCropp is a small yet powerful tool that empowers researchers to automate mundane image processing tasks, allowing them to focus more on their core scientific analysis.

docs.title: MycoDataLab - Data Management for Biological Research
Overview
docs.text:
MycoDataLab is a data management software designed to streamline and organize the recording of research data across different experimental processes. During my research on scab disease in guava and through collaborations with colleagues in various biological studies, I recognized the need for a cohesive system to efficiently record and visualize relationships between different experimental data points. In response, I developed MycoDataLab as a versatile solution tailored for biological research.

The software is built with a React frontend using Semantic UI for a clean and responsive user experience, and it leverages Python Flask as the backend for API services.

docs.title: Key Technologies
docs.text:
• Frontend: React with Semantic UI
  • Backend: Python Flask
  • Data Storage: JSON-based schema for flexibility in form definition
  • Mapping: Integrated map view for location data visualization

docs.title: Features & Modules
docs.text:
MycoDataLab is composed of several interconnected modules, each designed to handle specific types of research data. These modules ensure that researchers can maintain clear, structured records throughout different stages of their experiments:

  1. Location Data Manager
  2. Input and manage data related to field locations where samples are collected.

  3. Visualize entered locations on an interactive map.

  4. Sample Data Manager

  5. Record details about collected samples.

  6. Select associated locations from a dynamically populated dropdown menu, ensuring consistency and ease of use.

  7. Culture Data Manager

  8. Document and track cultured samples, including conditions and outcomes.

  9. Link sample records for a comprehensive data trail.

  10. Microscopy Data Manager

  11. Record details of microscopy observations, capturing various parameters and linking them to relevant samples and cultures.

  12. Bioassay Data Manager

  13. Manage bioassay experiments and outcomes, linking assays to relevant sample and culture data for streamlined analysis.

  14. Sequencing Data Manager

  15. Record and manage sequencing data, linking records to corresponding samples or cultures to maintain traceability.

docs.title: Custom Form Definitions
docs.text: One of MycoDataLab's key features is its flexibility in data entry. Since different researchers and studies have unique data requirements, the software utilizes a JSON schema to define form fields. Researchers can create custom forms tailored to their specific needs, ensuring that all relevant data points are captured.

docs.title: Interconnected Data Visualization
docs.text: The modules within MycoDataLab are interconnected to provide a holistic view of the research data. For example: - When entering sample data, users can select a location from a dropdown menu that automatically populates based on the available entered locations. - The map view allows users to see the geographic distribution of samples, providing valuable insights into the spatial relationships between data points.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
The current version of MycoDataLab focuses on core data management and inter-module connectivity. Future plans include: - Advanced data visualization options for generating graphs and reports. - Collaboration features to allow multiple researchers to work simultaneously on projects. - API integrations for connecting with external data analysis tools.

MycoDataLab is designed to empower researchers by providing a flexible, organized, and visual approach to data management, making it easier to maintain comprehensive records and gain insights into experimental relationships.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Rental Management System is a comprehensive web application designed to streamline and automate the management of rental equipment and machinery. It efficiently handles batch-level and unit-level inventory, providing a centralized platform for rental businesses to manage equipment records, track availability, schedule maintenance, and more. This system aims to simplify rental operations by reducing manual effort and increasing overall productivity.

docs.title: Inventory Management
docs.text:
• Batch and Unit-Level Tracking: Manages equipment at both batch and unit levels. Equipment units are associated with their respective batches, making it easier to track and organize assets.
  • Automatic SKU Generation: Automatically generates SKUs based on category and machine type codes for better identification and categorization.
  • Dynamic Equipment Info Modals: Provides detailed information modals for equipment units and batches, displaying all essential attributes.
  • Editable Equipment Data: Allows authorized users to edit equipment attributes such as brand, model number, serial number, and more at both batch and unit levels.
  • Filtering and Search: Offers extensive filtering capabilities based on attributes like brand, model, category, machine type, and warehouse location.

docs.title: Equipment Lifecycle Management
docs.text:
• Add and Remove Equipment: Provides the ability to add new equipment to existing batches, as well as edit, update, and delete equipment data as required.
  • Condition and Maintenance Tracking: Allows for tracking the condition of equipment over its lifecycle, including warranty and insurance expiration dates.
  • Supplier and Purchase Details: Maintains records of supplier details, purchase costs, invoice numbers, and other procurement information.

docs.title: Data Visualization and Reporting
docs.text:
• Data Grids with Inline Actions: Utilizes interactive data grids that allow users to perform actions like viewing, editing, and deleting records directly from the table view.
  • Summary Views: Displays an overview of key information, such as the total number of items in each batch and a summary of batch-level details.

docs.title: Security and User Management
docs.text:
• User Authentication and Permissions: Ensures that only authorized users can access, edit, or delete records through authentication and role-based permissions.
  • Audit Logs: Keeps track of all critical actions like equipment modifications, deletions, and additions for accountability and traceability.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
• React.js: Provides a dynamic and interactive user interface. Components like forms, tables, and modals are built using React for a seamless user experience.
  • Material-UI: Implements Material Design principles using MUI components for consistent styling and responsiveness. Features like DataGrid, Dialog, and Form components ensure high usability.
  • Axios: Handles asynchronous HTTP requests to the backend API for performing CRUD operations.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
• Django: A robust web framework that serves as the backbone for the server-side logic. Django REST Framework (DRF) is used to create a well-structured and modular RESTful API.
  • Django REST Framework (DRF): Manages endpoints for batch-level and unit-level inventory, allowing smooth data exchange between the client and the server.
  • PostgreSQL: Acts as the primary relational database for storing equipment records, batch information, and user details. PostgreSQL’s reliability and scalability make it an ideal choice for handling extensive inventory data.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The Rental Management System follows a modular monolithic architecture, organizing different modules by feature while maintaining a consistent codebase. The primary modules are:

  • Admin Panel: Allows admins to manage category information, warehouses, machine types, and other essential data.
  • Inventory Management Module: Handles all batch-level and unit-level CRUD operations, SKU generation, filtering, and data visualization.
  • User and Permissions Module: Manages user authentication and role-based permissions.

The system also integrates versioning of APIs to ensure backward compatibility and smooth feature enhancements over time.

docs.title: API Design and Endpoints
docs.text: The REST API has been designed with consistency and scalability in mind. It includes endpoints such as: - /api/inventory/v1/batches/: Handles CRUD operations for batch-level data. - /api/inventory/v1/units/: Manages unit-level operations like listing, updating, and deleting individual units. - /api/inventory/v1/units/list-all/: Provides a comprehensive view of all equipment units with batch-level context.

docs.title: Deployment and Scalability
docs.text: The application is containerized using Docker for consistent deployment and easy scalability. Nginx is employed as a reverse proxy, providing load balancing and SSL termination. The application is deployed on AWS EC2 instances with managed databases on RDS, ensuring high availability and fault tolerance.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The Rental Management System is a feature-rich, highly scalable, and secure platform that automates and simplifies rental equipment management. By leveraging modern frontend and backend technologies, the system provides an intuitive user experience and robust data handling capabilities. With a strong focus on flexibility, extensibility, and security, this system is an ideal solution for rental companies looking to streamline their operations and enhance productivity.

docs.title: SabraPoems - Android App for Literature Enthusiasts
Overview
docs.text:
SabraPoems was my first Android app, developed in 2019 to support students in the "Appreciation of English Literary Texts" course at the Diploma of English at Sabaragamuwa University of Sri Lanka. The app aimed to provide a convenient resource for students to access and explore a collection of recommended poems and related literature materials. The goal was to enhance the learning experience by centralizing essential poetry resources in a mobile-friendly format.

The app was built using HTML, CSS, Semantic-UI, JavaScript, and deployed through Apache Cordova for cross-platform compatibility. I hosted the app’s backend services on Heroku and successfully published it on the Google Play Store, where it garnered several tens of downloads.

docs.title: Key Technologies
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML, CSS, Semantic-UI
  • Backend: JavaScript, Heroku for deployment
  • Mobile Deployment: Apache Cordova
  • Design Framework: Semantic-UI for responsive and visually appealing design

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
1. Curated Collection of Poems The app featured a curated collection of poems recommended for the course. Students could easily browse and read the poems in a clean and organized layout, which was designed to enhance their reading experience.

  2. Links to Important Resources SabraPoems included links to external resources, such as critical analyses, literary commentary, and reference materials. This provided users with a comprehensive understanding of each poem’s themes, background, and stylistic elements.

  3. Simple and User-Friendly Interface Leveraging Semantic-UI, the app had a modern and minimalist design, making it easy for students to navigate and access the content they needed. The user interface was intentionally kept simple to avoid distractions while reading.

  4. Offline Access (Planned) While the initial version required an internet connection for some features, I planned to implement offline capabilities for accessing poems directly within the app without needing continuous connectivity.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: The inspiration for SabraPoems came from my own experiences and feedback from peers who faced challenges in accessing literary resources for the course. The idea was to create a mobile app that could serve as a portable literature companion, enabling students to engage with poetry anytime, anywhere. With the increasing use of smartphones among students, an Android app was a natural choice to deliver this convenience.

docs.title: Challenges and Learnings
docs.text: Being my first Android app, SabraPoems was a significant learning experience in mobile app development. Key takeaways included: - Understanding the integration of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with Apache Cordova for cross-platform mobile apps. - Learning to use Semantic-UI for responsive design and a visually appealing layout. - Managing app deployment on Heroku and handling basic backend tasks with JavaScript. - Publishing an app on the Google Play Store and understanding the nuances of app deployment and user feedback.

docs.title: Project Status
docs.text:
The app was successfully published on the Google Play Store in 2019 and achieved several tens of downloads. Although the codebase and screenshots are no longer available, SabraPoems remains a memorable milestone in my journey as a developer, reflecting my commitment to creating practical solutions for educational challenges.

SabraPoems serves as an example of leveraging technology to make learning more accessible and engaging, especially in the realm of literature and poetry.

docs.title: Car Price Scraper - Automating Price Comparison
Backstory
docs.text: As a car enthusiast and a tech-savvy problem solver, I often found myself comparing car prices across multiple classified sites. In Sri Lanka, two of the most popular platforms for used cars are ikman.lk and riyasewana.com. Manually comparing prices, filtering listings, and analyzing trends was not only tedious but also prone to errors. To solve this, I developed a Car Price Scraper, initially as a Python GUI application, and later upgraded it to a web application with a Flask backend and a React frontend.

docs.title: Technologies Used
docs.text:
• Python 3.x: The core programming language used for the application.
  • Tkinter: A standard GUI library in Python for creating graphical user interfaces.
  • Requests: A Python HTTP library used for sending HTTP requests to websites.
  • BeautifulSoup: A library for parsing HTML and XML documents, used here to parse web pages.
  • Pandas: A data analysis library used for data manipulation and analysis.
  • Threading: Python's threading module is used to run tasks in separate threads.
  • Concurrent Futures: Specifically, ThreadPoolExecutor for managing a pool of threads.
  • Logging: Python's logging module for logging events that occur during the execution of the program.

docs.title: GUI with Tkinter
docs.text:
The application uses Tkinter to create a graphical user interface. Key components of the GUI include:

  • Mode Selection: Allows users to choose between "CSV Mode" (loading data from CSV files) and "Scraping Mode" (scraping data from websites).
  • Output Frame: Displays messages and results to the user.
  • Buttons and Input Fields: Users can input search parameters, start/stop scraping, load data, and filter results.

docs.title: Multithreading
docs.text:
• Threading Module: The application uses the threading module to run the scraping functions in separate threads. This ensures that the GUI remains responsive while the scraping tasks are running.
  • Stop Flag: A threading.Event object is used as a stop flag to gracefully terminate the scraping process when the user requests it.
  • ThreadPoolExecutor: The concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor is used to manage threads that run the scraping functions for both websites concurrently.

docs.title: Web Scraping
docs.text:
• Requests Library: Used to send HTTP requests to the target websites and retrieve the HTML content.
  • BeautifulSoup: Parses the HTML content to extract relevant data such as price, brand, model, year, etc.
  • Respectful Scraping: The application includes time.sleep(1) calls to avoid overwhelming the target websites with requests.

docs.title: Data Handling with Pandas
docs.text:
• DataFrames: Scraped data is stored in Pandas DataFrames for easy manipulation and analysis.
  • CSV Export: DataFrames can be exported to CSV files for external use.
  • Filtering: Users can filter the data based on model name and mileage, and compute the average price.

docs.title: Mode Selection
docs.text:
Upon launching the application, users can select between:

  • CSV Mode: Load existing data from CSV files (ikman_cars_filtered.csv and riyasewana_cars_filtered.csv).
  • Scraping Mode: Scrape new data from the websites based on user-defined parameters.

docs.title: Scraping Parameters
docs.text:
In Scraping Mode, users can input the following parameters:

  • District: Selected from a dropdown list of districts in Sri Lanka.
  • Min Price and Max Price: Define the price range of the cars.
  • Brand: Specify the car brand (e.g., Toyota, Nissan).
  • Min Year and Max Year: Define the range of the year of manufacture.
  • Fuel Type: Choose from petrol, diesel, hybrid, or electric.
  • Transmission: Choose from automatic or manual.
  • Pages to Scrape: Specify the number of pages to scrape from each website.

docs.title: Start/Stop Scraping
docs.text:
• Start Scraping: Begins the scraping process in a separate thread to keep the GUI responsive.
  • Stop Scraping: Users can interrupt the scraping process at any time. The application uses a stop flag to gracefully terminate ongoing scraping tasks.

docs.title: Filtering Results
docs.text:
After scraping or loading data, users can:

  • Filter by Model Name: Enter a model name or part of it to filter the results.
  • Filter by Mileage: Specify minimum and/or maximum mileage to filter the cars.
  • View Results: The application displays the number of records after filtering and calculates the average price.
  • Save to a CSV

docs.title: Sporify: Automated Spore Measurement Application
docs.text:
❮ ❮ ❮ ❮ ❯ ❯ ❯ ❯

Project Type: Python GUI Application Technologies: OpenCV, PIL, Tkinter Purpose: Automating the measurement of Pestalotiopsis fungal spores.

docs.title: Backstory
docs.text: While researching the diversity of Pestalotiopsis fungi causing scab disease of guava in Sri Lanka, I encountered a significant challenge. To accurately characterize and measure the fungal spores, I needed to measure their length and width using microscopic images. However, the manual measurement process was incredibly time-consuming, with hundreds of images and numerous spores per image. The task was daunting, and I knew there had to be a better way. That's when I decided to create Sporify.

docs.title: Introducing Sporify
docs.text: Sporify is a custom Python GUI application specifically designed for automating the measurement of Pestalotiopsis spores in microscopic images. Built using OpenCV, PIL, and Tkinter, the application streamlines the entire process, allowing for accurate and efficient measurement of fungal spores.

docs.title: Key Features & Workflow
docs.text:
1. Calibration for Accuracy Before any measurements, Sporify allows users to calibrate the software using known units. A software like ImageJ can be used to find the calibration factor, which is then entered into Sporify as "pixels per μm" in the Calibration > Enter Calibration menu.

  2. Image Loading and Cropping Users can open a folder containing all the microscopic images via the File > Open Folder menu. Due to the round border created by the camera setup on the microscope, the application enables users to draw a square to select the region of interest, avoiding interference in the spore detection phase. This cropping is handled with PIL.

  3. Spore Detection Using OpenCV After cropping, Sporify processes the image using OpenCV techniques such as image thresholding and contour detection. This results in the identification of oval-shaped spores, which are displayed with green overlay lines to help users visualize the detected spores.

  4. Manual Refinement of Detection To ensure accuracy in scientific analysis, users can manually select the perfectly detected spores from the image. This flexibility is crucial as some spores may not be oriented correctly or fully detected.

  5. Measurement & Real-time Data Storage Once the selection is confirmed, Sporify measures the major-axis (length) and minor-axis (width) of the selected spores. The measurements are displayed in a table view on the right side of the interface. The software automatically loads the next image after each confirmation, making the workflow seamless. All measurements are saved to a CSV file in real-time, ready for statistical analysis.

  6. Streamlined Batch Processing Sporify processes images in sequence from the folder, allowing users to measure all images at once or quit midway, with the data saved continuously.

docs.title: Technologies Used
docs.text:
• Python: The backbone of the application.
  • OpenCV: For image processing, contour detection, and ellipse detection.
  • PIL (Pillow): For image manipulation, particularly cropping.
  • Tkinter: For building the graphical user interface.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
With Sporify, what was once a laborious and error-prone manual task became a streamlined and automated workflow. This application not only saved significant time but also improved the accuracy and consistency of my research measurements, enabling reliable scientific analysis.

Sporify is a testament to how technology can bridge the gap between traditional research methods and modern automation, enhancing the precision and efficiency of scientific investigations.

docs.title: WhatsApp Bot for Storing Lecture Recording Links
Overview
docs.text:
During the COVID-19 pandemic, as universities transitioned to online learning, lecture recordings became an essential resource for students. In the early days of online education, my university lacked a centralized method for storing and sharing these vital recordings. Different students recorded lectures on different days and shared Google Drive links in our WhatsApp groups. Over time, these links became buried under countless messages, making it difficult to locate the recordings when needed.

To address this challenge, I developed a WhatsApp Bot for storing and retrieving lecture recording links. The bot leveraged PHP and MySQL for backend processing and was connected to WhatsApp using an AutoResponder app. Users could interact with the bot using a specific message format to save and retrieve links efficiently.

docs.title: Key Technologies
docs.text:
• Backend: PHP-based API
  • Database: MySQL
  • WhatsApp Integration: AutoResponder for WhatsApp (an Android app to automate replies)
  • Hosting: A lightweight server to handle the PHP scripts and database

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
1. Centralized Database of Recordings The bot maintained a centralized database where users could store and retrieve lecture recording links. This eliminated the clutter and confusion caused by hundreds of WhatsApp messages with scattered links.

  2. Simple and Intuitive Commands Users interacted with the bot through simple, predefined commands. The message format was straightforward:

  3. To Retrieve a Link: GET SUBJECT-CODE DATE(DD-MM-YYYY) e.g., GET CS101 12-07-2020

  4. To Save a Link: SAVE SUBJECT-CODE DATE(DD-MM-YYYY) {Link} e.g., SAVE CS101 12-07-2020 https://drive.google.com/recordinglink

  5. Automated Response System The bot automatically parsed incoming messages and executed the corresponding database actions using a PHP-based API. The AutoResponder app on my phone handled the messaging interface, allowing users to interact with the bot through WhatsApp messages.

  6. Keyword-based Retrieval Users could search for lecture recordings by subject code and date, which made finding specific recordings much more efficient than scrolling through hundreds of WhatsApp messages.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: The motivation behind this project came from a clear gap in managing lecture recordings during the pandemic. With students struggling to find relevant recordings amidst a flood of WhatsApp messages, I aimed to create a solution that was simple, accessible, and reliable. WhatsApp was a widely-used platform among students, so using it as the primary interface made the bot easy to adopt.

docs.title: Challenges and Learnings
docs.text: Building the WhatsApp Bot was an exciting experience, particularly in learning how to automate interactions on a widely-used messaging platform. The project taught me how to: - Develop a structured API in PHP to handle database queries. - Design a simple and intuitive user interaction model based on message parsing. - Leverage AutoResponder to automate responses efficiently in a real-world messaging app.

docs.title: Project Status
docs.text:
The bot was actively used during the initial period of online learning, providing a valuable service to students by organizing and centralizing lecture recordings. Although the codebase and screenshots are no longer available, the project stands out as a practical solution to a real-world problem faced by students during the pandemic.

The WhatsApp Bot for Storing Lecture Recording Links showcases the power of integrating simple technology solutions into everyday communication tools to solve urgent challenges.
